get.summary: `GET /api/canvas?path=<path>` — read and validate a canvas document.
get.description:
Returns `{ canvas, rejected, kiln }`. Any node whose reference fails
containment is **redacted in the returned canvas** — a `file` node loses its
path, a `group` loses its background — and described in `rejected` so the UI
can render a quarantined placeholder explaining why.

This is the fail-safe layer. A `.canvas` hand-edited on disk to point at
`../../../etc/passwd` reaches this handler like any other, and the offending
path never leaves the process.

get.summary: The session's live event stream, resuming from a seq cursor.
get.description:
The body schema describes one SSE `data:` payload, not the whole stream:
OpenAPI has no way to say "many of these, one per line". Each event's seq
rides the SSE `id:` field, so a client that reconnects can name the last
event it applied — through `?after=` on a fresh `EventSource` (the browser
API cannot set headers) or the automatic `Last-Event-ID` a browser sends
when it retries the same source.

post.description:
The body and the answer are `config.save`'s own: `{values}` in,
`{ok, refused, rejected}` out. A refusal rides in the answer rather than in
an HTTP error because refusal is per leaf — the siblings the user changed

line the daemon named, which an error status cannot carry.

get.summary:
`GET /api/notes/resolve?kiln=<path>&name=<target>` — resolve a wikilink
target to a file, **by walking the kiln**.
get.description:
Deliberately independent of the note index. Opening `[[Some Note]]` is a
path question, and answering it from the index means a kiln that has not
been processed yet resolves nothing — which does not fail loudly, it falls
through to whatever kiln is configured as the default and silently opens a
same-named note from the wrong vault. Indexing is an optimisation for search
and backlinks; it must not be a prerequisite for following a link.

Resolution order, matching how wikilinks are written in practice:
  1. exact kiln-relative path (with or without the `.md` suffix)
  2. unique filename stem anywhere in the kiln

An ambiguous stem resolves to the shallowest match, which is the same
tie-break the link index applies.

# Isolation

**A root never resolves outside itself.** Every candidate is canonicalized
and checked against the canonical root, so a symlink planted inside one kiln
cannot surface a note from another kiln or from a project. Resolution
failing is the correct outcome — the alternative, quietly answering from a
different root, is how a link in one vault silently opens a same-named note
from another.

A path inside the root to search. The root that is actually walked is
the kiln or project this resolves to, never the supplied path itself.

get.summary: `GET /api/plugins/commands` — the executable primitives plugins declared.
get.description:
Each entry carries `plugin`, `name`, `description`, `hint`, `parameters`
and `effect`. The names are read, so the browser is told what a row holds;
`parameters` is passed through verbatim, so a caller offering a command as
a button — with a dialog built from the declared parameters — needs no
change on this side when a plugin ships a new one.

`parameters` crosses as opaque JSON today. It comes from the same
`ToolDefinition` a tool uses, so shaping it like `signature.rs`'s JSON
Schema output is what would let a dialog be generated rather than
hand-read — see `docs/Meta/Analysis/The Plugin Contract.md`.

The row type is `crucible_core::types::PluginCommand`, forwarded
unchanged: its `effect` field is `crucible_core::types::CommandEffect`,
the same closed vocabulary `crucible-lua` re-exports rather than mirrors.

Where `init.lua` and `settings.json` live, so a lock can offer a jump
to the file that holds a key. Absent when the daemon booted from a
config value rather than a file.

origins.description:
One row per recorded leaf, as `config.origin` gives them. The flat
shape is what a settings control renders a lock from; the effective
config's own `provenance` map is the same fact in the store's enum
shape, and serving both would be two spellings of one answer.

A closed shape, unlike the three fields around it: the daemon builds
every row from one type, so this route reads that type rather than
forwarding an object it cannot describe.

controls.description:
The declared control tree the settings UI renders, as
`config.controls` gives it: `{options, read_only}`. Served here rather
than from a second endpoint because a control and the value it shows
are one screen, and two fetches could disagree about which keys exist.

ConfigSaveReply.description:
What `config.save` answers.

A refusal rides in the answer rather than in an error: refusal is per leaf,
the siblings the caller changed in the same call did save, and `refused`
carries the file and the line a human's config holds the key on.

ok.description: Whether every leaf the caller sent reached the `Settings` layer.

refused.description: The leaves a pin refused, each with the source that holds it.

rejected.description:
The top-level keys that name where the daemon acts, which no save may
write. They are dropped rather than refused, so they are reported apart
from `refused`.

ContextStrategy.description:
Strategy for managing conversation context when it exceeds the token budget.

Serializes lowercase (`"truncate"`/`"summarize"`), matching [`FromStr`] and
[`Display`](std::fmt::Display) below. Before this type carried
`#[serde(rename_all)]`, the derive wrote the variant names as-is
(`"Truncate"`/`"Summarize"`) wherever a `SessionAgent` serialized this
field — including every session a daemon persisted to disk. The `alias`
on each variant keeps those old records loading: [`Deserialize`] accepts
either spelling, and [`Serialize`] only ever writes the new one.

CreateEntryParams.description:
`base.create_entry`: create a note that the base's filters admit.

`group` names the group the entry joins; JSON `null` is the group of
entries with no value.

kilns.description:
The session's kiln set by registry NAME — flat, no member privileged.
Empty or omitted is a literal empty set, NOT a request for a default:
it creates a session with no corpus attached. The daemon stopped
substituting its data root here because that root is the parent of the
sessions store, so "default" quietly put every transcript in scope.

endpoint.description:
Custom endpoint URL (optional, for self-hosted models). The daemon
refuses one that targets an internal address it does not have
configured.

agent_name.description: ACP agent profile name (e.g. "claude", "opencode"); required when agent_type == "acp"

agent_card.description: Internal-agent card name; never resolved in the web layer.

isolation.description:
Isolation override: absent → resolve normally; `false` → no container
even if the project has one; `true`, a profile name or an environment
object → override. Forwarded to the daemon untouched — the vocabulary
belongs to the plugin that resolves it, and an unknown profile comes
back as `-32602`, which `daemon_err` turns into a 422.

DelegationConfig.description: Delegation configuration for an ACP agent

enabled.description: Whether delegation is enabled for this agent

max_depth.description:
Maximum delegation depth: a delegation whose child would exceed this
depth is rejected. `max_depth = 0` disables delegation entirely;
`1` (the default) allows delegation but no nesting; `2` lets a
delegated child delegate once more, and so on. Depth is derived from
the child session's parent chain at every level.

allowed_targets.description: List of agent names this agent can delegate to

result_max_bytes.description: Maximum size of delegation result in bytes (default 51200)

max_concurrent_delegations.description: Maximum number of concurrent delegations a session can spawn (default 3)

timeout_secs.description:
Seconds a delegated child may run before it is cancelled (default 300).
Applies to blocking and background delegations alike.

DiffCommentKey.description:
One comment of the diffset of `source`: the request of
`diff.resolve_comment` and `diff.delete_comment`.

[`crate::diff::CommentRef`] names a comment too, but its wire field is
`id`. The two methods here send `comment_id`, so the shapes stay apart.
A key that the type does not know is refused, as in [`DiffCommentRequest`].

DiffCommentReply.description: What `diff.comment` answers: the stored comment and its diffset.

DiffCommentRequest.description:
Request for `diff.comment`: anchor a comment to a line range of one file
of the diffset of `source`.

A key that the type does not know is refused, not dropped. A caller that
sends a field of another shape, for example a `session_id`, learns of the
mistake. The web route reads this type, so the rule holds at each edge.

oneOf.description:
The absolute path of the root of the file. A session record and a
proposal need it, because each can have more than one root. A branch
source names its own root.

path.description: The path relative to the root, on the current side.

from.description:
The old path of a renamed file. A comment on the base side quotes
the text of this path.

side.description: The side that the line numbers count on.

line_end.description: One past the last line. Absent means `line_start + 1`: one line.

oneOf.description: Absent means a human wrote the comment.

DiffCommentsReply.description:
What `diff.comments` answers: each comment, oldest first, with its range
projected onto the current text of its side.

DiffFileEntry.description: One file of a diffset, with its counts and no text.

path.description: The path relative to `root`, as a `Comment` names it.

binary.description: The file is binary. It has no text.

too_large.description:
One side is larger than [`crate::types::acp::MAX_DIFF_BYTES`]. The
file has no text.

DiffFileText.description: The two texts of one file of a diffset.

Diffset.description: A set of file changes, without the text of the files.

unreadable_roots.description:
The roots that the diffset leaves out, because the daemon cannot read
them. Only a session record fills it. A branch and a proposal read
their files directly, so their list is empty.

DiffsetId.description:
The identity of one diffset.

The id derives from the source. Two requests for one source thus get one
id, and a client can use the id as the key of a tab.

oneOf.description: The merge base of `head` with `base`, to the working tree or to `head`.
The text before the first tool call of a session, to the files on disk.
One proposal. Its files are the files that it proposes to write.

DiffsetSource.description:
Where the two sides of a diffset come from.

This set is closed. The daemon has one exhaustive match on it, and the web
client has one.

success.description:
True when the daemon dropped the notification of the session, or hid
a shared notification for this session. False when the notification
does not reach the session.

oneOf.description: The expected text is not in the file. It moved on, or was never there.
The text appears more than once and the edit named no occurrence.
`occurrence` named a match the file does not have.
Two edits in one batch cover the same lines.
`expect` was empty, which would match everywhere and nowhere.

EditRefusal.description: Why one edit could not be applied. The index is the caller's edit index.

hint.description: Optional hint for what to focus on.

command.description: The command line, with or without its leading slash.

oneOf.description: The write replaces the disk text with no check.
The file must not exist. A file on disk is a conflict with an empty base.

The disk text must hash to `hash`. A stale base answers `current_hash`,
because the writer has no text to merge from.

The disk text must be `text`. A stale base merges `text`, the new
text and the disk text.

ExpectedBase.description:
The disk state that a write expects to find before it writes.

The wire fields `base_hash` and `base_text` map to this type. The type
keeps an absent file and an empty file different: `Absent` expects no
file, and `Text` with an empty text expects an empty file.

FileConflict.description:
A merge conflict in one file of a proposal.

The regions point into `merged_text`, so a client shows them with no
second merge.

disk_text.description: The disk text at the time of the merge.

merged_text.description: The text of the merge, with the proposed side in each region.

regions.description: Each cluster that the two sides changed differently.

FileDiff.description:
File diff representing changes to a file

Protocol-agnostic representation of file modifications. Can be populated
from ACP's `ToolCallContent::Diff`, generated from tool arguments, or
computed by comparing file states.

path.description: Path to the modified file

FileEntryRow.description: One entry of a kiln's file listing.

name.description: The file stem, or the whole path when the stem is not UTF-8.

path.description: RELATIVE to the kiln root.

is_dir.description:
Always `false`: this listing walks the note index, which holds files.
The key stays because the file tree reads one entry type for every
source, and `GET /api/fs/list` does report directories.

oneOf.description: The file moved. `from` is the old path, relative to the same root.

FileStatus.description: How a file changed between the two sides.

oneOf.description:
A whole write whose base was stale and whose merge left a region the
two sides disagree about. Nothing was written.

current_hash.description: BLAKE3 of the file as it is on disk NOW.

current_content.description:
The disk's text, so the caller can resolve without a second read
that would race the same way.

merged_content.description: The merge's own text, conflicts included.

regions.description: Every cluster the two sides disagree about.

oneOf.description:
A patch the daemon refused. `failed` is empty when the base alone
refused the batch, before any anchor was read.

stale_base.description:
Whether the file moved on since `base_hash` was read. `false` means
the anchors themselves refused.

oneOf.description:
A whole write whose base was stale and which sent no `base_text`, so
there was nothing to merge with. Nothing was written.

FileWriteConflict.description:
What a write answers when it refuses with 409.

Untagged, and the variant order is load-bearing: serde takes the first that
fits. Each arm names a field the others do not have — `regions` for a merge
that could not settle, `failed` for a refused patch, `error` for a bare
refusal — so the three are disjoint and
`a_conflict_reads_back_as_the_arm_that_was_sent` asserts each direction.

FileWriteResponse.description:
What a write answers when it lands.

One type for `PUT` and `PATCH`, because the daemon builds one object for
both: a patch never merges, so it writes no `merged` key, and a whole
write always does.

ok.description:
Always `true` here. A `false` carries a 409 and one of the
[`FileWriteConflict`] shapes instead.

merged.description:
Whether the caller's base was stale and its text was merged with the
disk. Absent on a `PATCH`, which never merges.

content.description:
What was written, present only when `merged` is `true`. The caller
holds it nowhere else: its own text is not what landed.

content_hash.description:
BLAKE3 of what was written, so the caller needs no second read to
learn the hash its next write must name.

FocusedNoteRow.description: The note the panel is about.

path.description: As the index holds it: kiln-relative in normal operation.

abs_path.description:
The same note joined onto the kiln root, which is what
`GET /api/kiln/file` takes.

title.description: The empty string when the index holds no title. Never `null`.

FsEntry.description:
One directory entry in an `fs.list_dir` response.

Wire keys (`name`/`rel_path`/`is_dir`/`size`/`modified`/`status`) are
byte-identical to the TypeScript `FsEntry`. `status` is a Phase-1 decoration
seam and is always `None`.

modified.description:
Unix epoch seconds, or `null` when the platform cannot report it.
Always written.

status.description:
The git/diff decoration seam. Always `null` today, and deliberately
open: whatever fills it will not be a string.

FsEvent.description:
A filesystem change delivered to the browser.

Serializes with an internal `type` tag whose values are `changed` /
`deleted` / `moved` (e.g. `{"type":"changed","path":"/abs","kind":"modified"}`).
The SSE `event:` name is separate — see [`FsEvent::event_name`].

FsListing.description:
One directory level, plus whether the cap cut it short.

Both keys are part of the cross-language contract (TypeScript `FsListing`).
The response used to be a bare array, which had nowhere to say "there is
more" — so a capped listing would have been indistinguishable from a complete
one, which is worse than the slow response it replaces.

FsMkdirResponse.description:
What `POST /api/fs/mkdir` answers.

The route's own shape, not the daemon's: `fs_mkdir` reports success as
`()`, so there is no daemon body to forward.

created.description: Always true. A refusal is an error status, not a `false`.

FsMoveReply.description:
What `fs.move` answers.

The two link-report keys are absent for a move the link index does not
watch — a directory, an asset, a project file — which is the shape the
browser already reads. They were written as a `json!` literal beside the
handler, where nothing held them to the reply the web route promises.

moved.description: Always true. A move that did not happen is an error, not a `false`.

rewritten_sources.description:
Sources whose inbound links were rewritten. Kiln note and canvas moves
only. Absent, never null, for a move with nothing to report.

skipped.description:
Inbound links left as they were, with the reason for each. Absent,
never null, for a move with nothing to report.

root.description: Absolute path of the root that holds both ends.

kind.description: Selects the allowlist that the daemon checks `root` against.

from_rel.description: Root-relative POSIX path of the entry to move.

to_rel.description: Root-relative POSIX path that the entry takes.

FsPathRequest.description: Request for `fs.mkdir` and `fs.trash`: one path inside one root.

root.description: Absolute path of the root that holds the entry.

kind.description: Selects the allowlist that the daemon checks `root` against.

rel_path.description: Root-relative POSIX path of the entry.

FsRootKind.description:
The two roots that an `fs.*` mutation may name, and the allowlist that
each one selects.

This type describes the wire, and the field that carries it is this type,
not a `String`: an unknown kind now fails at deserialize, where the
document's own error names the bad value, before a handler ever sees the
request. A web test still walks an exhaustive match over the two
variants, so a third kind cannot reach the document without a decision
about it.

trashed.description: Always true. A refusal is an error, not a `false`.

trash_path.description: Where the entry now sits, RELATIVE to the root it was trashed from.

GrepHit.description:
A single content-search hit.

`match_start`/`match_end` are **character** offsets into `text` (post-trim),
suitable for `<mark>` highlighting in the web UI. Only the first match on a
line is reported. Wire keys (`path`/`rel_path`/`line`/`text`/`match_start`/
`match_end`) are the `search_grep` RPC + `POST /api/search/grep` contract.

path.description: Absolute path to the matched file.

rel_path.description: Path relative to the search's `rel_base` (forward-slash separators).

text.description:
The matched line, trimmed of surrounding whitespace and capped at
[`GREP_SNIPPET_CAP`] characters.

match_start.description: Character offset of the first match's start within `text`.

match_end.description: Character offset of the first match's end within `text`.

GrepSearchRequest.description:
Request for `search_grep` (ripgrep-style content search).

`root` must resolve inside a registered project or open kiln — the daemon
rejects anything else. `glob` filters by file name (e.g. `*.md`); `None`
searches all files.

regex.description:
Compile `query` as a regex (Rust regex syntax) instead of matching it
as a literal substring.

limit.description: The handler still clamps this to `1..=GREP_MAX_LIMIT`.

case_insensitive.description: Defaults to `true`, which is what the handler's `optional_param!` did.

GrepSearchResponse.description:
Result of a `search_grep` call: the hits plus whether they were capped at
the requested limit. Matches the `POST /api/search/grep` response body.

write_value.description:
The `value` of the `base.set_property` call that puts a row into this
group, in the form the note stores. Null means "delete the property".

additionalProperties.description:
Per-tool permission level declared by an agent card.

Serialized forms accepted (matching the documented card format):
`true`/`"allow"` → Allow, `"ask"` → Ask, `false`/`"deny"` → Deny.

ImageFit.description: How a cards or kanban cover image fills its box.

oneOf.description: Question with optional choices.

allOf.description: Batched questions with "Other" text input option.

oneOf.description: Batched questions with "Other" text input option.
Artifact editing.
Display content (no response).
Permission request.

allOf.description: Popup with rich entries (for scripted popups).

oneOf.description: Popup with rich entries (for scripted popups).

allOf.description: Interactive panel (core primitive for scripted UI flows).

oneOf.description: Interactive panel (core primitive for scripted UI flows).

InteractionRequest.description:
Unified interaction request type.

This enum wraps all interaction primitives for use in event systems
and channels.

InteractionRespondResponse.description: The answer this route gives when the daemon took the response.

ok.description: Always `true`. A refusal is an error status, not a `false`.

oneOf.description: Response to an ask request.

allOf.description: Response to a batched ask request.

oneOf.description: Response to a batched ask request.
Response to an edit request.
Response to a permission request.
Response to a popup request.
Response to an interactive panel.
Request was cancelled by the user.

response.description:
The answer, in the kind-tagged shape `InteractionResponse` takes.

Open, because the vocabulary belongs to the daemon's interaction types
and an unreadable answer must come back as this route's 400 naming the
deserialiser's own complaint, not as axum's plain-text rejection.

InteractivePanel.description:
An interactive panel request.

This is the core primitive for scripted UI flows. Scripts provide items
and hints; the TUI renders an interactive list with filtering, selection,
and optional key handler callbacks.

Higher-level patterns (question sequences, fuzzy search, wizards) are
built on top of this primitive in script-land.

# Example

```
use crucible_core::interaction::{InteractivePanel, PanelItem, PanelHints};

let panel = InteractivePanel::new("Select database")
    .item(PanelItem::new("PostgreSQL").with_description("Full-featured RDBMS"))
    .item(PanelItem::new("SQLite").with_description("Embedded, single-file"))
    .hints(PanelHints::new().filterable());
```

header.description: Header/prompt text displayed above the panel.

oneOf.description: What a person, a plugin or a relay asked.
The notes that Precognition gave this turn, when it ran.

One run of answer text, with the reasoning that came before it. A
tool call ends a segment; the text after the tool is a new segment.
The token use of the turn, on its last segment.

model.description:
The model that the session used when the segment started, from
the last `session_initialized` or `model_switched` event.

terminate.description: The tool asked to end the turn.

outcome.description: The summary of a finished delegation, or the error of a failed one.

oneOf.description: Context that the session accepted for a turn. It is not a user turn.

`delegation_id` and `child_session_id` always hold the same value —
`DelegationSpawned` documents `delegation_id == child_session_id`. Both
are on the wire because a subscriber may read either, and dropping one
would silently break it.

data.description:
`delegation_id` and `child_session_id` always hold the same value —
`DelegationSpawned` documents `delegation_id == child_session_id`. Both
are on the wire because a subscriber may read either, and dropping one
would silently break it.

JobPayload.description:
Delegation and background-job lifecycle.

The `delegation_*` names predate the current delegation system and are
preserved for subscriber compatibility.

content_hash.description:
BLAKE3 of the bytes just read, so a later write can say whether the
file moved on. NOT the index's hash, which lags a save.

KilnFilesResponse.description:
What `GET /api/kiln/files` and `GET /api/kiln/notes` both answer.

One type for two routes because they answer the same projection of the same
listing. The key is `files` on both, including on the one named for notes.

KilnGraphLink.description: One edge of the `kiln.graph` note-link graph.

source.description: The linking note's path. Always a `path` in [`KilnGraphReply::notes`].

target.description:
The linked note's path when `resolved`; otherwise the target as it
was written, which names no note.

resolved.description: Whether `target` resolves to a note the caller can see.

KilnGraphNote.description: One node of the `kiln.graph` note-link graph.

path.description: Kiln-relative, and the value a resolved link's `target` joins against.

title.description: Never empty: the daemon falls back to the file stem.

KilnGraphReply.description: What `kiln.graph` answers: the full note-link graph of a kiln.

KilnListResponse.description:
What `GET /api/kilns` answers. A thin wrapper, not a copy: the row is
core's own [`KilnRow`], the same type `kiln.list` answers.

KilnRow.description:
One kiln, as `kiln.list` reports it.

Every key is written on every row, including the two an older reader
treated as optional, so this reply carries no absent-versus-false
ambiguity.

path.description: Where the kiln lives. This is the one listing whose job is to say so.

name.description:
The registry key — the name every other API call answers to. An open
directory that no entry names carries the empty string, never `null`.

registered.description:
Whether the registry answers for this directory, and therefore
whether `name` is a name an attach accepts. A row with `false` must
not be offered in a picker.

open.description:
Whether the daemon holds the kiln open right now. A closed row is not
a dead one: the first request that addresses a kiln opens it.

last_access_secs_ago.description:
Seconds since the daemon last touched the kiln, or `null` when it
holds it closed. Always written, so `required` rather than optional.

git.description:
Whether the kiln path is the top level of a git working tree. A
folder below the top level answers `false`, because `diff.get`
refuses it.

KnobRow.description:
One setting and whether this session can change it.

Mirrors `crucible_core::types::KnobDescriptor`, for the reason
[`WriteModeRow`] gives.

supported.description:
`false` means the control should not be offered: the daemon refuses
the call.

oneOf.description: The model id, as `session.switch_model` used to carry it.

value.description: The model id, as `session.switch_model` used to carry it.

oneOf.description:
The mode id. `None` is the agent's default mode: no mode was ever
set.

value.description:
The mode id. `None` is the agent's default mode: no mode was ever
set.

oneOf.description:
The strategy. A closed set, not a `String`: an unknown spelling now
fails at deserialize, where the wire's own error names the bad value,
instead of reaching the daemon's own `FromStr` check.

value.description:
The strategy. A closed set, not a `String`: an unknown spelling now
fails at deserialize, where the wire's own error names the bad value,
instead of reaching the daemon's own `FromStr` check.

oneOf.description: Whether the kiln is searched before the first message.

value.description: Whether the kiln is searched before the first message.

oneOf.description: Maximum consecutive plugin turns before approval becomes Ask.

value.description: Maximum consecutive plugin turns before approval becomes Ask.

KnobValue.description:
One knob and the value to read or write.

`session.knob.set` carries this as its whole body: the tag names the
knob, so a client that sends `{"knob": "mode", "value": "plan"}` cannot
name a knob and then send the wrong value's shape. `session.knob.get`
answers the same type, so a client reads a value the same way it wrote
it.

One variant per [`SessionKnob`] entry, and the compiler proves the two
enums stay matched: [`Self::knob`] has no wildcard arm, so a
[`SessionKnob`] variant added without a matching [`KnobValue`] variant
fails to compile here, not at run time.

LayoutWriteResponse.description:
What a layout write answers.

`POST` and `DELETE /api/layout` answer the same object, because both say
only that the file on disk now reflects the request. One type keeps them
from separating.

ok.description: Always true. A failed write is an error status, not a `false`.

allOf.description:
The source that owns the leaf, with its file and line when it has
them.

pinned.description:
Whether a boot-restored layer holds this leaf, so `config.save`
refuses it.

LeafOrigin.description:
Where one leaf came from, and whether `config.save` would refuse it.

The row `config.origin` answers with. `pinned` is the refusal rule itself,
reported per leaf, and the [`SourceOrigin`] beside it is the pin that
refuses — the same one the refusal carries. See [`crate::config::ConfigStore::origin`]
for why the pin, and not the last writer, names the file here.

LineRange.description:
A half-open range of 1-based line numbers.

`start == end` is a valid empty range and is how a pure insertion is
expressed on the *before* side (and a pure deletion on the *after* side).

end.description: One past the last line, 1-based, exclusive.

LinkSuggestion.description: A single suggestion to convert a plain-text mention into a wikilink.

mention.description: The text that was found as a mention (preserves original casing)

target.description: The note name to link to

offset.description: Byte offset in the text where the mention starts

ListedComment.description: A comment as the daemon lists it: its range follows its text.

comment.description: The stored comment. When its text moved, `line_range` is the new range.

outdated.description:
The current text of the side does not contain the quoted text.
The pane shows an outdated comment at the end of its file.

Mark.description:
A row's status, stated as a fact rather than as a glyph.

The plugin says what is true. The TUI may draw `●` and the web a coloured
dot; each client picks its own mark. A plugin that shipped its own glyph
would bind one client's medium into a contract both must honour, which is
the mistake this enum exists to prevent.

port.description: The SSE port, or `null` under stdio. Always written.

kiln_path.description: The kiln path the server serves.

finished.description:
Whether the server task has already finished, which is how a crashed
server reads while the manager still calls itself running.

oneOf.description:
A server is serving a kiln. Listed first so a payload that carries the
running keys never reads as the stopped arm, which ignores them.
No server is running.

McpStatus.description:
What `mcp.status` answers: the server is up, or it is not.

Untagged, because the two arms are told apart by `running` and the wire
has always spelled them that way. The stopped arm carries `running` ALONE:
a stopped server has no transport, no port and no kiln, and writing those
keys as null would say it has them and they are empty.

MergeRegion.description:
A cluster both sides changed differently.

The lines are 1-based and the end is exclusive, the convention
`crate::session::types::review::LineRange` uses, and they point into the
MERGED text, so a reader can show the region without diffing again.

start_line.description: First line of the region in the merged text, 1-based, inclusive.

end_line.description:
One past the last line of the region in the merged text, exclusive.
Equal to `start_line` when our side deleted the cluster.

base.description: The cluster as the base held it.

ours.description: The cluster as our side wrote it. This is what the merged text holds.

theirs.description: The cluster as their side wrote it.

ModeRow.description:
One mode a session may enter.

Mirrors `crucible_core::types::mode::ModeDescriptor` field for field, for
the reason [`WriteModeRow`] gives.

name.description: The label to draw.

icon.description: An emoji or an icon name.

writes.description:
What a note write in this mode does, already degraded to what this
session's agent can hold back.

ModelsResponse.description:
Response for model listings — the session-scoped `list_models` and the
session-less `list_all_models` return the same `{ models: [...] }` shape.

kiln.description:

The one session it belongs to, when the engine reported it for that

present for a set and ignored otherwise.

One interaction a session is waiting on an answer to.

Permission to read a file/directory.
Permission to write a file/directory.
Permission to call a tool.

Request permission for an action.

Supports token-based pattern building for vim-style permission UIs
where users can expand/contract the permission scope.

File diffs for this permission. Empty for non-file actions or when
the diff couldn't be synthesized at the daemon (e.g. file too large
or `old_string` not found in disk content).

The permission layer that asked the user, for example

Scope for permission grants.

Determines how long a permission grant remains valid.

A repository top level, as `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` printed it.

The source that holds the leaf, with the file and line when it has

A bare acknowledgement: `plugin.option_set` and `plugin.option_execute`

A permission floor a plugin can add to its turns.

`EnumIter` gives the menus of both clients every value, so a new value
reaches them without a second list.

One executable primitive a plugin declared, and the arguments it takes.

The declared parameters, as the JSON Schema `signature.rs` emits, or
`null` for a command that takes none.

Declared by the plugin and verified by nothing. A consumer must
present it as a claim, and a permission layer must treat it as a hint
about what to ask — never as permission to skip asking.

One discovered plugin, as `plugin.list`'s `plugin_info` rows describe it.

Every discovered plugin, not only the healthy ones: a plugin that failed to
load carries its reason in `last_error`, and dropping it would make

`None` when the plugin has no fragment, or its fragment names no
version. The daemon always writes the key, so `required` rather than
optional.

Where the plugin came from: `User`, `Runtime`, `EnvPath` or `Builtin`.
A plain string, because this writes `Display` output rather than a
serde spelling.

The lifecycle state: `Active`, `Error` or `Disabled`. A plain string
for the same reason as `source`.

Why the plugin is not `Active`, or `None` for a healthy one. Always
written, so `required`.

The plugin also activated on the running daemon.

`installed: true` with `loaded: false` is a plugin that reached the
disk and broke on load; `error` says why, and the next boot tries
again. A client must not read `installed` alone as success.

Why the plugin did not load, or `None`. Always written, so
`required`.

A sentence about hot reload. The watcher's list is a boot-time
snapshot, so a plugin installed at runtime works but is not
rewatched.

manifest.description:
The installed manifest the entry was written to
(`plugins.installed.json`).

PluginListResponse.description:
What `GET /api/plugins` answers.

The daemon's own `plugin.list` reply carries this same data under

renames it to `plugins`, which is the key the plugins panel has always

The answer to `action: "set"` and `action: "execute"`.

PluginOptionCallReply.description:
What one option call answers: a value for a `get`, an acknowledgement for
a `set` or an `execute`.

Untagged, because one web endpoint (`POST /api/plugins/{name}/option`)
serves three RPC methods with three different reply shapes.

**The variant order is load-bearing.** Serde takes the first variant that
fits, so a union whose first variant also fits the second's bodies reads
every one of them as the wrong thing. These two are disjoint: neither
field has a default, so `{"ok": true}` has no `value` and `{"value": …}`

Whatever the plugin's getter returned, and `null` is an answer.

Opaque: an option's type belongs to the plugin, and the renderer reads
the value against the node that declared it.

PluginOptionsReply.description:
What `plugin.options` answers: one settings tree per plugin.

**A deliberate narrowing to the envelope.** The tree itself stays opaque,
and that is not laziness about a shape nobody wrote down — the nodes are
fully described in `crucible-lua`'s `describe_node`. It is about numbers:

The plugin that was removed, as the manifest named it.

kept_dir.description:
Removed without a purge, and the directory is still there. It sits in
a permanent search path, so the next daemon start discovers and loads
it again. `None` when nothing is left behind, which is the only case
where "removed" means gone.

result.description:
Whatever the command's Lua `fn` returned.

Opaque, like publications and options: what a command returns is the
plugin's vocabulary, and a shape validated here would be one only
today's plugins could send.

Whatever the command's Lua `fn` expects. `null` when the caller sends
nothing; the command then gets an empty table.

The session the user ran the command from, when there is one. The

session" does not need the user to type an id.

The version the plugin declares, or `None` while nothing has read it.

Enumeration does not run a plugin's Lua, and the version lives in the
spec table that only a load reads — so a discovered plugin has no
version to report. This field carried a synthesized `"0.0.0"` there,
which every front end drew as if it were a release.

Search relevance score from the vector index. Defaults for payloads

A proposal changed. The browser reads it again through

Where a wikilink target landed.

browser has read that spelling since before this route was typed, and
renaming it would break the editor's open-a-link path for no gain.

ResumeSessionResponse.description:
What `POST /api/session/{id}/resume` answers, which depends on the path
that resumed the session.

The warm path answers the state change. The cold path reloads the session
from the store and answers its history, because that call is also what

holds the order.

not used here: these are daemon replies, and refusing a field a newer
daemon added would turn an extension into a 502 on three healthy routes.

SemanticSearchRequest.description:
`POST /api/search/semantic` — text semantic search over a kiln's notes.
Embeds the query with the kiln's embedding provider, then cosine-scans the
embeddings in the kiln's SQLite store. Two daemon RPCs (`embed.query` +
`search_vectors`) mirror the CLI's `run_semantic_search`. The daemon
answers with one row per block, best first. The panel lists notes, so
this route keeps one row per note: its best block, with `block` and
`snippet` when the kiln has block rows. Each hit's `document_id` is the
kiln-relative note path; `path` is the absolute path for the editor to
open. Requires an embedding provider (else `embed.query` fails) AND
processed notes (no embeddings yields no hits).

kiln.description: Absolute path of the kiln to search.

SemanticSearchRow.description: One note hit, with the block that earned it.

document_id.description:
The note's kiln-relative path. The same value as `rel_path`; both stay
because the browser reads both.

rel_path.description: The note's kiln-relative path, for display.

path.description: The absolute path, which is what an editor opens.

oneOf.description:
The note's best block, or `null` when the kiln has no block rows.
Always written.

snippet.description: The block's text, or `null` when there is none. Always written.

comments.description:
Stored review comments that the message attaches. The daemon builds
the context of each one, and refuses an unknown or resolved comment.

oneOf.description: A turn started. Its events follow on the session's event stream.

The text named a command that the daemon ran without a turn, for
example a plugin command or a bare mode switch.

SessionAgent.description:
Agent configuration bound to a session.

This captures everything needed to reconstruct an agent when resuming
a session. The configuration is inlined (not just a reference) so that
sessions are self-contained and reproducible.

agent_name.description: ACP agent name (e.g., "opencode", "claude") - only for ACP agents

provider_key.description: Provider key (e.g., "ollama", "openai", "anthropic") - only for internal agents

system_prompt.description: System prompt (full text, inlined from agent card if applicable)

env_overrides.description: Environment variable overrides for ACP agents

mcp_servers.description: MCP servers this agent can use

agent_card_name.description: Source agent card name (for reference, not used for reconstruction)

agent_description.description: Human-readable description of this agent (from ACP agent profile)

oneOf.description: Delegation configuration for this agent (from ACP agent profile)

precognition_enabled.description: Whether Precognition (auto-RAG) is enabled for this session (default: true)

context_budget.description: Context window token budget. None = no limit.

context_strategy.description: Strategy for truncating context when over budget.

mode.description:
Session mode id ("ask" | "plan" | "auto"). Persisted so a mode set
before the first message (no live handle yet) still applies when the
agent handle is created, and survives handle eviction. `None` = normal.

oneOf.description:
Per-tool permission policy from the source agent card. Deny = tool
not advertised and refused; Ask = always prompt; Allow = never
prompt. Tools not listed use default behavior. `None` = no policy.

name.description: The name after the slash.

input_hint.description: The argument placeholder, when the command takes one.

SessionCommand.description: One entry of a session's command catalog.

continued_from.description: The session this one continues, when it continues one.

oneOf.description: The session's full agent record, when the session has an agent.

plugin_approvals.description:
Per-plugin approval state. Every session record has this map, empty
or not.

plugin_turn_limit.description:
Turns a plugin-started session may run before the daemon stops it.
Every session record has a value, defaulted if never set.

oneOf.description: How the session records its transcript, when it has a recording mode.

SessionDetail.description:
The full session record, as `session.get` answers it: every
[`SessionSummary`] field, flattened onto the wire, plus the fields a
caller needs to start a session like this one.

event.description: The event name, such as `user_message` or `text_delta`.

data.description:
The event payload. Its shape follows `event` — see
[`crate::protocol::session_events::SessionEventPayload`] for the
typed union. Untyped here on purpose: a stored transcript replays an
event name a newer daemon minted, which this build cannot type.

transcript.description:
What the event changed in the folded transcript of the session. The
daemon sets it on the live copy only: the stored log holds the events,
and a reader folds them again. A client that renders the transcript
applies these ops; it does not fold the event itself.

SessionEventPayload.description:
A decoded session-event payload: one of eight groups.

Construct with [`SessionEventMessage::typed`](crate::protocol::SessionEventMessage::typed);
read with [`SessionEventMessage::payload`](crate::protocol::SessionEventMessage::payload).
`ToSchema` reads the bare `#[serde(untagged)]` below even though this
enum derives no `Serialize`: [`SessionEventPayload::to_wire`] is what
actually serializes it, and it always yields one of the eight groups'
own `{event, data}` shape, never a wrapper around one — which is what
`untagged` documents to a reader of `openapi.json`.

SessionHistoryResponse.description:
What `GET /api/session/{id}/history` answers.

`history` is the core [`crucible_core::protocol::SessionEventMessage`] —
the same envelope the SSE stream carries — replayed whatever the
transcript holds, including an event name a newer daemon minted. Its
`data` stays untyped for exactly that reason: this build cannot type an
event it does not know.

history.description: The page of events the query asked for.

total_events.description: How many events the whole transcript holds, for paging.

transcript.description:
The whole log, folded into what a client draws. The daemon folds it;
a client renders it and does not fold the events again.

SessionId.description:
A session identifier that is safe to join onto a directory.

Guaranteed by construction to be a single, ordinary path component:
non-empty, no separators, no `.`/`..`, no NUL, no leading dot, and drawn
from `[A-Za-z0-9._-]`. See the module docs for why that matters.

kilns.description:
The session's kilns, by registry name.

Was `kiln_path: PathBuf` — the resolved directory of whichever kiln
happened to sort first, produced by `kiln_paths(..).next().unwrap_or_default()`.
It was broadcast to every subscriber and persisted into `session.jsonl`
whenever the session already had an agent config at create time.

A set, not one member: kilns are flat, so there is no "the" kiln to
report. Empty means the session reaches no kiln — never "unconstrained",
and never the empty path, which every path helper reads as the daemon's
own data directory.

`workspace_path` beside it stays a path: the agent runs commands there,
so the directory is the fact being reported.

knobs.description:
Every knob Crucible has, answered for. A client that finds an id
missing is talking to an older daemon.

previous_state.description: The state the session left. `session.end` does not send it.

state.description: The state the session is in now.

kilns.description: The session's kilns. Only `session.end` sends them.

SessionListReply.description:
Reply from `session.list`.

One `SessionSummary` per session, listing-shaped: see
`crate::session::SessionSummary` for which fields a listing fills.

total.description: How many sessions the reply carries.

current_mode_id.description: The mode the session is in. Always one of `modes`.

modes.description: Every mode the session may switch to, in declaration order.

notifications.description:
The daemon's notifications of the session, newest first, each with
`id`, `kind` and `message`, as `notification_added` carries them.

SessionScopeResponse.description: The session scope that a kiln or workspace mutation echoes.

kilns.description: Every kiln the session can query, by registry name.

workspace.description: The session's working directory. `null` is a session with no workspace.

SessionSearchMatch.description:
One transcript line that matched a session search.

Not a session: the daemon answers the line it matched on, so a caller that
wants the session reads `session_id` and asks for it.

line.description:
The 1-based line of the transcript. `0` marks a title match on a
session whose transcript has not reached disk yet.

context.description: The matched line, truncated to 100 characters.

total.description: How many matches the reply carries.

note.description:
Why the search looked at nothing, when it looked at nothing.

The daemon writes it for a search with no kiln scope, and only then.
An unscoped search is the one case where an empty result is not a
statement about the corpus, so the sentence has to reach the caller.

SessionStatusResponse.description:
What `GET /api/session/{id}/status` answers.

Each item is the daemon's [`StatusDisplayItem`], the same type that the
`status_items_changed` event carries, so the browser and the TUI read one
shape. `id`, `plugin` and `text` stay plain strings: the moment a client
enumerates them, a new plugin needs a client change to be visible at all,
which is the thing this channel exists to avoid.

[`StatusDisplayItem`]: crucible_core::types::StatusDisplayItem

status.description:
Every item the session has, ordered by priority. A session with no
item answers an empty list.

SessionSummary.description:
Summary of a session for listing. The one core reply shape for
`session.list` and `session.create`.

A lighter-weight version of Session without full event history.

session_id.description: Session ID. The wire name is `session_id`, never `id`.

type.description: Session type, sent as its lowercase prefix (`"chat"`, `"agent"`, …).

kilns.description: Kilns this session can query, by registry name. See [`Session::kilns`].

workspace.description: Workspace, when the session has one. See [`Session::workspace`].

started_at.description: When the session started. Every session has one.

title.description: The session title, when one has been set.

event_count.description: Number of events in the session.

agent_model.description: Agent model name (for display), when the session has an agent.

last_activity.description:
Last activity timestamp, when the session has run at least once.
Absent for legacy sessions that predate the field.

parent_session_id.description:
Parent session id for delegated child sessions, when this session is
one. `#[serde(default)]` keeps old meta files valid.

SessionType.description: Type of session, determines logging format and behavior.

SetPropertyParams.description:
`base.set_property`: set or delete one frontmatter property of a note.

`value` present, including JSON `null`, sets the property; `null` writes
an empty property, as Obsidian does. An absent `value` needs
`delete: true`, so that a forgotten value never deletes a property.
The key `file.folder` moves the note into the folder that `value` names.

oneOf.description:
`data.mode` is the field the web SSE mapper and the TUI reducers read —
keep the name stable.

data.description:
`data.mode` is the field the web SSE mapper and the TUI reducers read —
keep the name stable.

oneOf.description:
The session's scope after a change: its kilns by registry name, and
its workspace (`null` for a session with no workspace).

data.description:
The session's scope after a change: its kilns by registry name, and
its workspace (`null` for a session with no workspace).

oneOf.description:
A plugin's approval knob changed. `approval` is the knob's own
spelling (`inherit`, `ask`, `stop`).

data.description:
A plugin's approval knob changed. `approval` is the knob's own

oneOf.description:
The session's ACP agent advertised a new command list. A client
reads the catalog again with `session.commands`. A plugin reload

SettingsPayload.description:
Session-settings events, adjacently tagged so the enum's serialization *is*

oneOf.description:
The ACP agent refused `session/resume`, so the daemon opened a new
agent session, and the agent does not have the earlier history.

Live only: the EventBus gives it a seq and journals it, and
`is_persisted` keeps it out of `session.jsonl` as for the other
setup notices. The connection fact belongs to this daemon run, and
the next connection reports its own disposition.

SetupPayload.description:
Setup-phase events, adjacently tagged so the enum's serialization *is* the
`{event, data}` pair the envelope carries.

`context_limit_resolved` is the one that is not exclusively a setup event.
A delegated agent has no endpoint or model for the daemon to query, so its
window arrives mid-turn instead (ACP `usage_update` →
[`TurnEvent::ContextWindow`](crate::turn::TurnEvent::ContextWindow)) and the
daemon re-emits the same event from the turn stream. Consumers treat it as a
plain assignment, so a late one needs no special case.

Shape.description:
What a client draws.

One variant, because one renderer exists. `Tree`, `Table` and `KeyValue`
arrive **with** their renderers, not ahead of them: the exhaustive match
on this enum is what forces that.

ShowRequest.description: Request to show content to the user (display only, no response).

SkillDetail.description: What `skills.get` answers: one skill, with the body a summary omits.

scope.description: The discovery scope the skill came from, as `SkillScope` spells it.

source_path.description: Where the skill file sits on disk.

agent.description: The agent the skill declares, when it declares one. Always written.

license.description: The licence the skill declares, when it declares one. Always written.

body.description: The skill's Markdown body, without its frontmatter.

SkillSummary.description:
One skill in a `skills.list` or `skills.search` answer.

The two RPCs answer the same row, because a list and a search are the same
question asked of two different sets. A second row type here would let one
of them grow a field the other cannot report.

name.description: The skill's name, which is also the key `skills.get` takes.

scope.description: The discovery scope the skill came from, as `SkillScope` spells it.

shadowed_count.description: How many same-named skills this one shadows.

SkipReason.description:
Why one inbound reference was left as it was.

A closed set, because the browser prints a sentence per reason. It was four
string literals spelled in five places, so a fifth reason could reach a
client whose reader has no arm for it. `every_skip_reason_reaches_the_wire`
(`crucible-web`) walks an exhaustive match, so a new variant fails to
compile until somebody decides what the client says about it.

SkippedRef.description: One inbound reference that was intentionally left untouched.

SourceOrigin.description:
Where one leaf came from, in the shape the wire uses.

One projection serves two callers: `config.origin` answers with it, and a
`config.save` refusal names the pin with it. Two projections would let the
refusal name a file the origin does not.
`Deserialize` as well as `Serialize`: `config.save`'s refusal travels back
over the RPC into a typed reply, and a `&'static str` cannot be read from a
document. The value is still [`ConfigSource::short`]'s, written once.

source.description: The one-word source name, as [`ConfigSource::short`] gives it.

file.description: The file the source names, when it names one.

line.description: The line inside `file`, when the source recorded one.

StatusColorGroup.description:
Names shared by status producers and both renderers. Unknown names render
as info.

One table: serde, strum and the OpenAPI schema all read the names below,
and `EnumIter` gives every consumer the complete set.

StatusDisplayItem.description:
The client-facing status item.

The one wire shape of a status item: the `session.status` reply and the
`status_items_changed` event both carry a list of it, and the web route
declares it in the OpenAPI document. The daemon keeps the authored list;
clients only decide where and how it fits.

text.description: The text to draw. The producer writes it; no client rewrites it.

priority.description: Smaller values appear first. Pinning is separate from the order.

color_group.description: Named color, which each client resolves through its own theme.

action.description: The engine method that the item opens, if it opens one.

pinned.description: A pinned item stays visible when the other items overflow.

plugin.description: The plugin that the item is about.

kind.description:
Who made the item. The TUI places each kind with its own statusline
item; the web draws every kind in one slot.

oneOf.description:
How far the work that the item describes is. `None` is a state
("sandboxed: alpine"), not a bar that stalls at zero.

StatusItemKind.description: The source of a status item.

oneOf.description: Fraction complete, clamped to 0.0..=1.0.
Work is underway with no meaningful fraction: draw a spinner.

StatusProgress.description:
How far along a status item's work is, when it is work rather than a
state.

Modelled on LSP `$/progress`: the producer reports and the client decides
how to draw it. An image pull knows its fraction; an image build does
not, and a fake fraction for the second is worse than saying so. On the
wire it is a number or the string `"indeterminate"`.

StopReason.description:
Reason a turn ended, carried on `TurnEvent::Done`.

It reaches a plugin on the `turn:complete` payload and a front end on
`message_complete`, so a handler can tell a model that finished from a
model the provider cut off. The host itself reads none of it: what to do
about a premature stop is the plugin's decision.

Two variants this deliberately does NOT have. A stop-sequence variant,
because Crucible sets no stop sequence anywhere, so no provider can report
one. A tool-use variant, because the turn loop emits `Done` only when no
tool call is pending — a provider that says "tool_use" has already had its
calls dispatched, and the turn after them ends for some other reason.

Surface.description:
One declared surface, as `surface.list` and `surface.get` report it.

Rows travel with the surface. A surface is a panel a person reads, not a
feed a client polls piece by piece.

plugin.description: The plugin that declared it, so a stale surface can be attributed.

name.description: The plugin's own name for it. Stable across a reload.

session.description:
The session this surface is about, or `null` when it is about the
plugin. Always written, so `null` means "about the plugin", never
"unknown".

version.description:
Bumped on every row change, so a client redraws on a change it sees
rather than on a timer.

SurfaceChangedEvent.description:
A surface changed, delivered to the browser.

Carries the identity and the new version, never the rows — the same contract
the daemon event has, and for the same reason: a surface is unbounded where an
event is not, and two clients want it at different moments. The browser
refetches through `GET /api/surfaces`.

withdrawn.description:
The surface is gone, so the browser drops it instead of refetching.

Passed through rather than re-derived. The daemon knew this when it
dropped the entry, and a browser that had to ask `GET /api/surfaces`
to find out would pay a round trip for a fact the event already held.

SurfaceListReply.description: What `surface.list` answers: every declared surface, rows included.

id.description:
Stable identity, chosen by the plugin. What an action names later, and
what a client keys a selection on across a re-push.

detail.description:
Secondary text, or `null` when the row has none. Always written, so
`null` means "no detail", never "unknown".

oneOf.description:
Status, or `null` when the row has none. Always written, so `null`
means "no status", never "unknown".

SystemEvent.description:
One frame of the system stream. The SSE `event:` name tells the two
shapes apart.

mapped everything that was not `created` to `Modified`, silently.
`path` is required, not defaulted: a file event without a path is
meaningless, and the consumer this replaces dropped such an event rather
than firing a handler on an empty path. `kind` defaults to `Modified`,
matching the two-arm string match it replaces.

The payload is the `ui.config` RPC result, produced by
`rpc::ui::style_payload` (theme, geometry, bars) or
`rpc::ui::expr_payload` (one session's statusline values). The two
genuinely differ in shape, so this stays a `Value`: a client applies it

oneOf.description:
A subscriber fell far enough behind the broadcast ring that events were
overwritten before it read them, and `dropped` of them are gone for good.

This is a *transport* fact rather than something that happened in the
session, and it is the one event the daemon emits about its own delivery.
It is in this vocabulary anyway, deliberately: it reaches clients over the
same channel as everything else and both surfaces render it, so leaving it
outside would mean exactly the untyped `{event, data}` pair this enum
exists to retire — and a marker announcing lost data is a poor thing to
leave unvalidated. Consumers should treat it as "your transcript has a hole
here", not as session content.

are a designed hook surface rather than a Rust variant name.

A session was created, reported daemon-wide.

Addressed to the system session, not to the new one, because the
audience is a client or plugin watching *every* session — a session
list, for instance — which is by definition not attached to the session
that just started.

oneOf.description:
A plugin's surface changed, so every client refetches it.

Carries the identity and the new version, never the rows. A surface is
unbounded where an event is not, and two clients want it at different
times, so the event says *what* moved and the client asks for the
content. This is what makes the version on the surface worth having.

withdrawn.description:
The surface is gone: stop drawing it, and do not refetch.

The one field that makes this event actionable on its own. Every
other change withholds the rows so the client asks; a withdrawal has
nothing left to ask for, and a client that had to re-derive it from
an empty refetch could not tell it apart from a lost race.

Omitted from the wire when false, so an ordinary change serialises
exactly as it did before this field existed.

oneOf.description:
A plugin's published data changed, so a client re-reads it.

Carries who published and under which key, never the value: a
publication is opaque JSON of the plugin's own choosing, and a client
that already holds the key refetches through
`GET /api/plugins/publications`.

Not an `EventName`, so no Lua handler subscribes to it: those are the
daemon events a plugin listens for, and this travels the other way —
plugin to client. A hook here would offer a plugin a handler on its own
writes, which is a loop waiting to happen.

oneOf.description:
A proposal changed: a proposal is new, it has a new write, or its
state changed.

The event carries only the id. A client reads the proposal again
through `proposal.get`. A proposal belongs to no user session, so the
daemon sends this event on the system session.

data.description: A session ended, reported daemon-wide. See [`Self::SessionCreated`].

SystemPayload.description:
Daemon-wide events that are not scoped to one turn: file-watch, kiln
processing, UI config, webhooks, replay.

cache_read_tokens.description: The prompt tokens that the provider read from its cache, when it said.

ToolRender.description:
Display data for one tool call. A render function makes it: a Lua
function for a kind, or [`ToolRender::fallback`].

It holds meaning, not terminal text and not HTML. Each client draws the
line and the fields in its own way.

line.description:
The one line that says what the call does, for example a command
line, a path, a URL or a query.

fields.description: The other facts of the call, in order.

summary.description:
The one line that says what the result is, for example `42 lines`.
Only the render of a finished call sets it.

result.description:
Arbitrary JSON: a string for most tools, an object for structured
ones. Never assume `as_str()`.

spill_path.description:
Set when the output was spilled to disk (≥10KB, spillable tool).
The referenced file lives under the session dir and outlives the
event, so this is the recovery path for the full output.

oneOf.description:
The render of the finished call. It replaces the render of
the call, and its `summary` says what the result is.

ToolResultBody.description:
The body of a `tool_result` event's `data.result`.

Untagged because the wire form has no discriminator: success is
`{"result": …}` and failure is `{"error": …}`, decided by which key is
present (`agent_manager/messaging/tool_call.rs`). The variants are disjoint
on their required key, so untagged is unambiguous — but they must stay
disjoint. A key added to both breaks the decode silently.

[`Systems`](../../../../../docs/Meta/Analysis/Systems.md) documented this as
"the `{"result"|"error": …}` envelope": a two-key description of a four-key
reality. `spill_path` and `render` are the other two.

Transcript.description: The folded transcript of one session.

as_of_seq.description:
The `seq` of the last event in the fold. A client drops each later op
whose event `seq` is not above it.

TranscriptFrame.description:
The second SSE frame for a live event that changed the transcript, with
the same `id:` as the event's own frame. The browser applies `ops` to the
snapshot the history route gave, and drops an op when `seq` is not above
the `as_of_seq` of that snapshot.

One variant, internally tagged on `type`, rather than a plain struct with
a hand-set `&'static str` field: a bare `&str` gives the schema `type:
string`, not the literal `"transcript"` a browser needs to discriminate
on. The tag is the whole reason for the enum.

id.description:
Stable across the live stream and a fold of the stored log: the turn
id for a user turn, `{turn}-seg-{n}` for an answer segment,
`tool-{call_id}` for a tool card.

turn_id.description: The turn that the item belongs to, when it belongs to one.

timestamp.description:
The time of the event that made the item. For an answer segment, the
time of the event that ended it: a stored log has no text deltas, so
only the end has one time in the live stream and in the log.

TranscriptItem.description: One thing that a client draws.

oneOf.description: Add the item, or replace the item with its id.

before.description:
For a new item: the id of the item it goes before. `None` puts it
at the end.

oneOf.description:
Add text to a field of a segment. `at` is the length of the field
before the text, so a client that missed an op sees the gap.
A person sent the message through a client.
The plugin with this name asked for the turn.

name.description: The plugin with this name asked for the turn.

oneOf.description:
A person wrote the message in the channel of the plugin with this
name (a relay, such as Discord). The turn is a user turn.

name.description:
A person wrote the message in the channel of the plugin with this
name (a relay, such as Discord). The turn is a user turn.

TurnOrigin.description:
Who asked for a turn.

A turn ENDS, and a `turn:complete` handler that wants more work asks for a
NEW turn. That turn is a normal turn: it takes admission, Precognition,
persistence and undo like any other. Only this field says who asked.

The serde form is the `origin` of the `user_message` event and of the
render payload: `{"kind": "plugin", "name": "goal"}` or `{"kind": "user"}`.

oneOf.description:
Context before this marker remains in the transcript but is excluded
from future model turns.

data.description:
Context before this marker remains in the transcript but is excluded
from future model turns.

oneOf.description:
Who asked for this turn. `None` and `User` both mean a person;
`None` keeps the wire of a person's message as it always was.

A text segment that streamed before a tool call, emitted at the
text→tool boundary. `message_id` is the turn id (shared with
`user_message` and `message_complete`); `index` is the 0-based segment
position within the turn; `content` is the segment's text (the delta
accumulated since the previous boundary). Lets viewers converge on
canonical per-segment bubbles across live streaming and history reload.
`message_complete` still carries the WHOLE turn's accumulated text —
segments are additive, not a replacement.

oneOf.description:
The five token fields are absent when the provider reported no usage,
and the two cache fields are absent when the provider reported no
caching. `skip_serializing_if` is what keeps that distinction on the
wire — a client tells "no data" from "zero" by presence, and the TUI
status bar's sentinel depends on it.

data.description:
The five token fields are absent when the provider reported no usage,
and the two cache fields are absent when the provider reported no
caching. `skip_serializing_if` is what keeps that distinction on the
wire — a client tells "no data" from "zero" by presence, and the TUI
status bar's sentinel depends on it.

oneOf.description:
Why the turn ended. Absent for the same reason the token fields
are: no data rather than a default. A turn whose stream closed
without a terminal `Done` has no reason to report, and every
`session.jsonl` line an older daemon wrote predates the field.

stop_notice.description:
The note a client draws under a reply the provider cut off, in
the words of [`crate::turn::StopReason::user_notice`] — the
daemon words it once, here, so that a client with no access to
the wording, such as the web page, need not repeat it. Absent
when the reason needs no note, which is every normal turn.

oneOf.description:
Field order is load-bearing: `serde_json` is built with
`preserve_order`, so the declaration order here is the key order on the
wire and in `session.jsonl`. It reproduces the insertion order of the
`json!` block this variant replaced — `display` after `source`, not
next to `args`.

data.description:
Field order is load-bearing: `serde_json` is built with
`preserve_order`, so the declaration order here is the key order on the
wire and in `session.jsonl`. It reproduces the insertion order of the
`json!` block this variant replaced — `display` after `source`, not
next to `args`.

oneOf.description:
The canonical tool call with its render, so the TUI and the web
draw the same table instead of each rebuilding the call.

Every producer in this workspace sets it. `None` means the event came
from something else — a recording made before the field existed (only
7 of 97 recorded `tool_call` lines carry it), or a foreign emitter —
and the consumer falls back to its own heuristic.

auto_approved.description:
Which layer granted permission without asking, if any. Rides on this
event rather than a follow-up: the gate decides BEFORE the card is
emitted, so a separate event would only make the marker pop in late.

oneOf.description:
A new canonical form of a tool call that a prior `tool_call` already
announced. An ACP agent can send the arguments or the diff of a call
in a later frame. Subscribers replace `args` and `display` of the
entry with `call_id`. A `display` with no render carries only the
diffs of an old transcript (see [`super::migrate`]), so the card keeps
its line.

data.description:
A new canonical form of a tool call that a prior `tool_call` already
announced. An ACP agent can send the arguments or the diff of a call
in a later frame. Subscribers replace `args` and `display` of the
entry with `call_id`. A `display` with no render carries only the
diffs of an old transcript (see [`super::migrate`]), so the card keeps

auto_approved.description:
Which layer granted the call without asking. An ACP agent asks
after it announced the call, so the marker comes in an update.

oneOf.description:
`terminate` is serialized even when `false` — an existing subscriber
reads `data.terminate` unconditionally. Do NOT add
`skip_serializing_if`.

`result` is the nested [`ToolResultBody`] envelope, kept as a `Value`
here because a recorded `tool_result` may carry any shape and the event
must still decode. Use [`ToolResultBody::of`] to read it.

reads `data.terminate` unconditionally. Do NOT add

`result` is the nested [`ToolResultBody`] envelope, kept as a `Value`
here because a recorded `tool_result` may carry any shape and the event

result.description:
The success/failure envelope. Typed for the schema as
[`ToolResultBody`]; still decoded as `Value` at runtime so a
shape neither variant covers still reaches a client — see
[`ToolResultBody::of`].

oneOf.description:
The whole turn is over. The daemon sends it exactly once for each
turn, as the last event of the turn, after the request slot is free.
A client ends a turn on this event, not on `message_complete`.

`status` has no default: an event that does not say how the turn
ended tells a client nothing.

data.description:
The whole turn is over. The daemon sends it exactly once for each
turn, as the last event of the turn, after the request slot is free.
A client ends a turn on this event, not on `message_complete`.

`status` has no default: an event that does not say how the turn
ended tells a client nothing.

oneOf.description: The stop reason of the last provider call, when it sent one.

error.description:
The error text for `failed` and `timed_out`, and the reason for
`handler_cancelled`.

oneOf.description:
Context that the session accepted for its next turn. It is not a
user turn.

The daemon stores it in `session.jsonl` on its own ordered path, as
the turn accepts it; the broadcast writer does not store it again.

data.description:
Context that the session accepted for its next turn. It is not a
user turn.

The daemon stores it in `session.jsonl` on its own ordered path, as
the turn accepts it; the broadcast writer does not store it again.

tags.description: The tags that a `transform_context` handler finds the block by.

kind.description:
The kind of the injection, for example `context` or `plugin`.
Absent for plain context.

source.description: Who injected it: a plugin name, `rpc`, or a diffset source.

after_turn.description:
The message id of the turn whose input was already assembled
when the context arrived. A reader places the context before
the next turn after it. Absent: before the next turn after the
line itself.

notes.description:
Absent when the search found no notes. Older recordings carry
`[]` for that case, and the decode reads both.

oneOf.description:
The same payload goes to the subscribers and to the Lua
`post_llm_call` handlers (`messaging/stream.rs`).

data.description:
The same payload goes to the subscribers and to the Lua
`post_llm_call` handlers (`messaging/stream.rs`).

TurnPayload.description:
Turn-stream events, adjacently tagged so the enum's serialization *is* the
`{event, data}` pair the envelope carries.

TurnStatus.description:
How a whole turn ended.

The daemon sends it in the `turn_finished` event and gives it to the
in-process caller of `send_message_notified`. [`StopReason`] tells why ONE
provider call stopped. This tells what happened to the turn.

UnreadableRoot.description:
A root that a diffset leaves out, and the reason.

The session record compares each root with its session base. When the
root or its base snapshot is gone, the record cannot list the files of
that root. The client shows the root, so that the user does not read the
record as complete.

reason.description: Why the daemon cannot read the root, as a sentence for the user.

kiln.description: Absolute path of the kiln to search.

vector.description: The query vector, already embedded by the caller.

VectorSearchRow.description: One block hit, as `search_vectors` ranked it.

oneOf.description:
Where in the note the hit sits, or `null` when the hit names the whole
note. Always written, so `null` reads as "the whole note" and never as
"unknown".

ViewOptions.description:
Built-in presentation options, projected from preserved Obsidian view data.
Every field has its default, so clients do not repeat them.

WebhookReceiveReply.description:
What `webhook.receive` answers.

Acceptance only: the delivery became a `webhook:received` event, and
whether a plugin was listening is not this answer's business. Every refusal
is an HTTP error at the ingress route, which never reaches this RPC.

WikilinkTarget.description: One wikilink target, as [`NoteByNameReply::wikilinks`] reports it.

WorkflowPayload.description:
Workflow-engine progress.

Every name needs an explicit `rename`: the wire uses a `workflow.` prefix
that `rename_all = "snake_case"` cannot produce.

`WorkflowCompleted` and `WorkflowCancelled` are **empty struct variants, not
unit variants**. Under adjacent tagging a unit variant omits `data`
entirely, which `to_wire` then reports as `null`; today's producers emit
`{}`. `{}` and `null` are different JSON.

WorkspaceChoice.description:
The body of `session.set_workspace`, inside `Scoped`.

`workspace: None` detaches.

workspace.description:
The workspace path. An absent or `null` value detaches: the session
then has no workspace.

WriteErrorRow.description: The error envelope a bare stale-base refusal carries.

code.description: The HTTP status, repeated in the body.

WriteModeRow.description:
What a note write in a mode does.

Mirrors `crucible_core::types::mode::WriteMode`, which carries no
schema: `crucible-core` takes no utoipa dependency, and a client that
shows a mode has to know the values it can read.

oneOf.description:
The disk holds the change. `ancestor_hash` is the hash of the file now,
for the next write.

The file already said what the write asked for, so nothing was
written: an equal value, or a base that already exists.
The session proposes the write; the disk is unchanged.
The file changed since the caller read it.
A permission rule or a `base:before_write` policy refused the write.
